prompt.context_jp: 独りが好きで理屈っぽい建築家、桑野信介の事務所には、この夜も薄暗い明かり___灯っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 独りが好きで理屈っぽい建築家、桑野信介の事務所には、この夜も薄暗い明かり___灯っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits here.

feedback.correct_en: This is a scene-setting description introducing a new element (the dim light) into view. New-information subjects in narration take が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame 'the dim light' as a known topic being contrasted or commented on — unnatural for first mention in scene description. を would require a transitive verb.

contrast_examples.jp: 部屋に明かりがついていた。
contrast_examples.en: A light was on in the room. (new info)

contrast_examples.jp: その明かりは暗かった。

prompt.context_jp: 村上が桑野に話している場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 桑野さんが招待されたパーティーに 俺だけ___来て 変でしょう？
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits with 俺だけ here?

feedback.correct_en: '俺だけが' exhaustively identifies who shows up — 'only I' (and no one else). This exhaustive-listing use takes が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は after だけ would weaken the exclusive focus; the speaker is emphasizing that he alone, uniquely, would be the attendee.

prompt.context_jp: パーティー会場にて。
prompt.prompt_jp: 桑野___愛想笑いを浮かべもせずに、壁ぎわで英治の営業ぶりを冷ややかに眺めていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks 桑野 here?

feedback.correct_en: Kuwano is the established topic of this scene — the narrative continues commenting on what he does. Topic continuity → は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would reintroduce him as new information, but he's already the known protagonist being described.

contrast_examples.jp: 桑野は壁際に立っていた。
contrast_examples.en: Kuwano (as topic) was standing by the wall.
It was Kuwano who was standing. (identification)

prompt.context_jp: 英治が蘊蓄を披露している場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: その受け売り___、皮肉なことに桑野の耳にも届いてしまう。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits best?

feedback.correct_en: The 'hearsay' is introduced as an event — it reaches Kuwano's ears. This is a neutral-description subject taking が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make it a topic being contrasted, but here the sentence simply reports what happens.

prompt.context_jp: 建築家にとって営業は避けて通れぬ仕事だが、...
prompt.prompt_jp: 建築家にとって営業は避けて通れぬ仕事だが、桑野___面倒な社交には端から興味を示さない。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: The sentence contrasts Kuwano's attitude with what architects generally should do. 'As for Kuwano...' — contrastive/topical は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark him as a newly-identified subject, losing the contrast the だが sets up.

contrast_examples.jp: 他の人は行くが、彼は行かない。
contrast_examples.en: Others go, but he (in contrast) doesn't.

prompt.context_jp: パーティー中、桑野の視線に気づいた瞬間。
prompt.prompt_jp: 桑野の気配に気づいた紀子___、はっと顔を上げた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle introduces 紀子 here?

feedback.correct_en: Noriko is being introduced as the one performing a sudden action in the scene — new-information subject → が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would treat her as an established topic; she's just now entering focus as the actor of this sudden movement.

contrast_examples.jp: 紀子は振り向かなかった。
contrast_examples.en: Noriko (as for her) didn't turn around.

prompt.context_jp: 桑野がスパゲティについて説教している。
prompt.prompt_jp: スパゲティっていうの___ 直径 約1.9ミリの物をいうんですよ
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: This is a definition — 'As for what we call spaghetti, it refers to...'. Definitions use は to set the topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would wrongly frame spaghetti as new information rather than the topic being defined.

prompt.context_jp: 部屋の空気が張りつめた直後。
prompt.prompt_jp: 桑野信介その人___、いま姿を見せたのだ。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: Dramatic entrance: 'It was Kuwano himself who appeared.' Exhaustive/identifying が highlights that this very person has now shown up.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make it a continuation of an existing topic, losing the dramatic 'here he is!' effect.

prompt.context_jp: 事務所の日常について。
prompt.prompt_jp: 桑野の毒舌___よって商談が一瞬で流れることは、月に一度は起きているのだった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle completes によって?

feedback.correct_en: The fixed causative/agent phrase is Xによって ('due to X / by X'). The particle is always に.
feedback.incorrect_en: によって is a set expression; でよって doesn't exist.

contrast_examples.jp: 台風によって中止になった。
contrast_examples.en: It was cancelled due to the typhoon.

prompt.context_jp: 摩耶が反論する。
prompt.prompt_jp: 私___だって理想はあんのよ
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits with 私 here?

feedback.correct_en: '私にだって理想はある' = 'Even I have ideals.' The dative に marks the experiencer of 'having' here, strengthened by だって.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would clash with だって in this construction; 'to me too' needs に.

contrast_examples.jp: 子供にだって権利がある。

prompt.context_jp: 同じ夜のこと。
prompt.prompt_jp: 同じ夜、桑野___自室で図面に集中していたが、やがて腹の底に鋭い痛みを覚えた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: Kuwano is the established protagonist; the narration continues with him as the topic across clauses. Topic は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make him a newly identified subject, but he's already in focus from the surrounding narration.

contrast_examples.en: He was reading a book. (topic continuation)

prompt.context_jp: 救急隊員とのやり取り。
prompt.prompt_jp: ジョウナンダイ病院___ あと どれぐらいかかる？
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: 'How much longer until (we reach) Jonandai Hospital?' marks the endpoint with まで.
feedback.incorrect_en: に would mark direction but not the 'until-reaching' sense; から is the starting point.

prompt.context_jp: 母親の育代が息子に。
prompt.prompt_jp: あなた___死なれたら 孫の顔が見られなくなるでしょう
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits here?

feedback.correct_en: The 'suffering passive' construction 〜に死なれる ('to have [someone] die on one') marks the deceased with に.
feedback.incorrect_en: は or が would break the passive-of-suffering pattern; に is required to mark the person who dies.

contrast_examples.jp: 子供に泣かれて困った。
contrast_examples.en: I was troubled by my child crying (on me).
I had my parent die on me.

prompt.context_jp: 母親が本音を語る。
prompt.prompt_jp: ただ 孫___欲しいって言ってるの
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: The adjective 欲しい takes が to mark the desired object. 'What I want is a grandchild' — が also conveys exhaustive focus.
feedback.incorrect_en: を is used with verbs like 欲しがる but not with the adjective 欲しい. は wouldn't fit the 'what I want' pattern here.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼は水を欲しがっている。

prompt.context_jp: 佐川が夏美に語る。
prompt.prompt_jp: 実際 教授の奥さん___ お医者さんが多いでしょう？
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: 'As for professors' wives, many are doctors.' This is the classic 'topic + descriptor-が' double-subject construction; the outer noun takes は.
feedback.incorrect_en: Two がs in a row here would be unnatural — you need は to set the topic frame and が to mark the inner subject (多い).

prompt.context_jp: 英治が桑野に営業するよう頼む場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 近々 家 建てたいって人が いるんです たまには___してくださいよ
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the blank with the best fit.

feedback.correct_en: 営業する specifically means 'to do sales / solicit business from clients' — exactly what Eiji is scolding Kuwano to do.
feedback.incorrect_en: 仕事する is too generic ('work'). 商売する refers to running a business, not pitching to a prospect.

prompt.context_jp: 夏美が去り際に桑野に言う。
prompt.prompt_jp: ちょっとは キャラ___ないと 孤独になりますよ
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in with the best verb phrase.

feedback.correct_en: キャラを考え直す = 'rethink your character/personality.' 考え直す is the natural verb for reconsidering a trait or decision.
feedback.incorrect_en: 思い直す is more for changing one's mind about an action; 見直す means to reassess value, not to overhaul personality.

contrast_examples.en: I changed my mind about going.

prompt.context_jp: みちるが友達に愚痴る。
prompt.prompt_jp: ただ"ひどい上司だね"って ___になってほしかったの
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in.

feedback.correct_en: 味方になる ('to take one's side / be an ally') is the exact phrase for wanting emotional support in a dispute.
feedback.incorrect_en: 仲間 means peer/comrade; 友達 is friend. Neither captures 'take my side against someone.'

prompt.context_jp: 夏美が照れる桑野に。
prompt.prompt_jp: 私は医者です ___ことないんですよ
prompt.prompt_en: Which fits best?

feedback.correct_en: 〜がる + ことない = 'no need to act embarrassed.' がる converts an adjective of feeling into an outward behavior.
feedback.incorrect_en: 恥ずかしいことない would mean 'it's not embarrassing' — different meaning. 恥 alone doesn't fit the grammar.

prompt.context_jp: 夏美が中川との交渉案を提示する。
prompt.prompt_jp: それで手を___ませんか？
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the verb.

feedback.correct_en: 手を打つ = 'reach a settlement / strike a deal.' Idiomatic for proposing a compromise.
feedback.incorrect_en: 手を組む means 'join forces'; 手を引く means 'withdraw.' Neither fits a 'let's settle on this' proposal.

prompt.context_jp: 英治が隣人に手土産を渡す。
prompt.prompt_jp: ああ これ ___ 物ですけど どうぞ
prompt.prompt_en: Which humble phrase fits?

feedback.correct_en: つまらない物ですが is the set humble phrase when offering a gift in Japanese — 'just a trifling thing, but please.'
feedback.incorrect_en: Saying 安い物 ('cheap thing') would be rude; 少ない物 doesn't exist as an expression.

contrast_examples.jp: つまらない物ですが、どうぞ。
contrast_examples.en: It's nothing much, but please accept it.
Just a token of my feeling.

prompt.context_jp: 壁際で冷ややかに眺める桑野を描く地の文として。
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds more natural as narration?

choices.text: 桑野は愛想笑いを浮かべもせずに、壁ぎわで英治の営業ぶりを冷ややかに眺めていた。
桑野が愛想笑いを浮かべもせずに、壁ぎわで英治の営業ぶりを冷ややかに眺めていた。

feedback.correct_en: In extended narration where Kuwano is the established protagonist, は flows naturally across the clause boundaries.
feedback.incorrect_en: が here would sound like a sudden spotlight on a new subject, jarring in continuous narration.

contrast_examples.en: It was he who was silently watching. (identificational)

prompt.context_jp: 桑野が『そのうち見ます』に返す皮肉。
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural as Kuwano's cynical retort?

choices.text: そのうちなんつって 見たヤツは ほとんどいませんよ
そのうちと言って 見た人は ほとんどいないです

feedback.correct_en: The casual sneer requires the colloquial なんつって and ヤツ to deliver Kuwano's mocking tone. The actual line uses this register.
feedback.incorrect_en: The polite rewrite flattens the sarcasm — too neutral for a dismissive jab at a party guest.

contrast_examples.jp: そのうちなんつって、やらないんだよ。
contrast_examples.en: 'Eventually,' yeah right — they never do it.

contrast_examples.jp: 後でやると言って、結局やらない人が多い。
contrast_examples.en: Many say they'll do it later but never do. (neutral)

prompt.context_jp: 桑野がクライアントに『先生』と呼ばれた直後。
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds more natural for Kuwano here?

choices.text: この間も言いましたが、"先生"と呼ぶのはやめてください
この間も言ったけど、"先生"って呼ぶのやめろ

feedback.correct_en: Kuwano is blunt but maintains です/ます with clients. The actual line balances his pedantry with professional distance.
feedback.incorrect_en: The plain-form version would be too rude even for Kuwano in a business context — he saves blunt commands for Eiji.

prompt.context_jp: 桑野が苦しみながら隣人に返す皮肉。
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural as Kuwano's sarcastic reply?

choices.text: いいように見えますか？

feedback.correct_en: To a stranger (neighbor he hasn't really met) Kuwano still uses ますか form — matches the actual line and the social distance.
feedback.incorrect_en: The plain-form か would be too familiar for a first interaction with a neighbor he doesn't know.

prompt.context_jp: 桑野が夏美の『あなたのポリープにまだ用がある』に返す場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which response better matches Kuwano's pedantic humor?

choices.text: 僕のポリープは 用がないって言ってます
僕のポリープは何も言っていません

feedback.correct_en: Kuwano mirrors her metaphor (giving his polyp a voice) to parry — the rhetorical echo is what makes the line characteristically him.
feedback.incorrect_en: The literal denial loses the game of volleying the personification; it would sound flat and un-Kuwano-like.
